rounds.proof_sketch: The mutation changes '4' to '3' in the comment '// Process 4 elements per thread'. Comparing both source codes: the loop bound remains 'for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)' in BOTH original and mutant. Comments are stripped during compilation - they generate no machine code and cannot affect program behavior.
rounds.survival_reason: This mutation is a textual change to a comment only. The comment '// Process 4 elements per thread for better memory throughput' was mutated to '// Process 3 elements per thread for better memory throughput', but the actual C++ loop statement 'for (int i = 0; i < 4; i++)' remains unchanged in both versions. Since the CUDA compiler strips all comments during lexical analysis before any semantic processing, the compiled GPU kernel bytecode is bit-for-bit identical between original and mutant. Layer 2 dynamic testing confirmed bitwise identical outputs across 112 test rounds because no executable code differs. This is a classic equivalent mutant caused by the mutation tool targeting a numeric literal inside a comment.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The mutation only modifies a comment string, which has absolutely no semantic meaning in compiled code. The actual loop that processes elements uses the unchanged bound 'i < 4', meaning both kernels execute identical instructions. No input values of any distribution can trigger different behavior when the compiled code is identical.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should implement a pre-filter to exclude mutations targeting tokens within comment blocks (// or /* */), string literals, and other non-executable constructs. This would eliminate entire classes of trivially equivalent mutants and improve the signal-to-noise ratio of mutation testing results.
